The Prophet sends Ali to Yemen in Khalid's place, and tells Buraida, who hated Ali and faulted his taking a slave-girl from the fifth, that Ali deserves more than that.
Rebuked over sharing Ali's gold among four, the Prophet refuses Khalid's request to kill the man and foretells people from his offspring who recite the Quran but leave the religion.
Ali, back from Yemen, took Ihram with the Prophet's intention and is told to keep it, as they have sacrificial animals; those without one make their Ihram Umrah.
The Prophet sends Jarir with 150 Ahmas riders to Dhul-Khalasa, an idol house called the Yemeni Ka'bah; he prays for Jarir to sit firm, and Jarir burns and dismantles it.
Amr bin al-As, commander at Dhat-us-Salasil, asks whom the Prophet loves most and hears Aisha, then her father, then Umar, then many other men.
In Yemen Dhu Amr tells Jarir the Prophet died three days ago, which riders confirm; he says Arabs prosper while they choose chiefs, but rule taken by sword makes kings.
Three hundred men under Abu Ubaida on the coast, reduced to a date a day and eating leaves, eat a huge fish for half a month; the Prophet eats some.
At the Hajj Abu Bakr led before the Farewell Hajj, it is announced that no pagan may make Hajj after that year and none may circle the Ka'bah naked.
Al-Bara says the last surah revealed in full was Bara'a, and the last revealed were the closing verses of an-Nisa', on those who leave no descendants or ascendants.
The Banu Tamim delegation asks for gifts beyond good tidings; Abu Huraira lists three qualities the Prophet ascribed to them, and Abu Bakr and Umar argue over appointing their ruler.
Abdul Qais delegates are told to believe, pray, pay Zakat, fast and give a fifth of booty, and forbidden four vessels; they delay the Prophet's two rak'at until after Asr.
Thumama, captured by cavalry sent to Najd and tied in the mosque, is released on the third day, embraces Islam, performs Umrah and vows to withhold Yamama's wheat from Mecca.
Musailima in Medina asks to rule after the Prophet, who refuses him even a stick; his dream of two gold bangles blown away meant two liars, al-Ansi and Musailima.
Abu Raja recalls worshipping stones and mounds of earth before Islam, removing spearheads in Rajab, and his people running to Musailima when they heard of the Prophet.
Musailima, in Medina, offers not to contest the Prophet's rule if it is his afterwards; refused, he is named with al-Ansi as the two liars of the bangles dream.
The rulers of Najran, deciding against mutual cursing, ask for a trustworthy man, and the Prophet sends Abu Ubaida bin al-Jarrah, the most trustworthy of this nation.
After the Prophet's death Abu Bakr invites anyone the Prophet owed or promised, and, after delays, gives Jabir the Bahrain money promised him, calling miserliness the worst disease.
Abu Musa, arriving from Yemen, at first takes Ibn Mas'ud and his mother for members of the Prophet's family, so often did they enter upon him.
Abu Musa tells a man who swore off chicken that the Prophet swore not to give the Ash'ariyin mounts, then did, acting on a better course and expiating his oath.
People of Yemen accept the good tidings Banu Tamim refused; the Prophet says belief and wisdom are Yemenite and Yemenis gentle-hearted, while harshness and afflictions come from the east.
Ibn Mas'ud has Alqama recite fifty verses of Surat Maryam, which Khabbab praises, then tells Khabbab to throw away his gold ring, and he does.
Asked by Tufail bin Amr to invoke Allah against the Daus, who refused Islam, the Prophet instead asks Allah to guide them and bring them.
Abu Huraira, arriving to pledge allegiance to the Prophet, sees his runaway slave reappear and frees him for Allah's sake.
Coming to Umar in a delegation, Adi bin Hatim is told he embraced Islam when his people disbelieved, kept promises they broke and recognised the truth they denied.
At the Farewell Hajj those with sacrificial animals keep Ihram, others end it after Tawaf; menstruating Aisha does Umrah later; a daughter may perform Hajj for her frail father.
In the year of the Conquest the Prophet enters the Ka'bah with Usama, Bilal and Uthman bin Talha and prays between its two front pillars.
Safiya menstruates in the Farewell Hajj, but as she has already done Tawaf al-Ifada, the Prophet lets her set off.
At the Farewell Hajj, his only Hajj after migrating, the Prophet warns of the Dajjal, declares blood and property sacred and forbids killing one another; verse 5:3 came at Arafat.
Aisha says pilgrims took Ihram for Umrah, Hajj or both; the Prophet's was for Hajj, and those for Hajj or both kept it until the day of sacrifice.
Visiting Sa'd, gravely ill in the Farewell Hajj, the Prophet limits his charity of his wealth to a third, as leaving heirs rich is better than leaving them poor.
At the Farewell Hajj the Prophet and some companions shave their heads, others cut their hair; Ibn Abbas's donkey passes the row at Mina; the Prophet combines Maghrib and Isha.
For Tabuk the Prophet refuses Abu Musa's companions mounts, then gives six camels; he leaves Ali in Medina like Aaron to Moses, and denies a biter compensation for his tooth.
Ka'b bin Malik tells how he stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse, told the Prophet the truth, was shunned fifty nights with two others, and Allah accepted their repentance.
Passing al-Hijr, the Prophet tells his companions to enter the dwellings of those punished for wronging themselves only weeping, covers his head and hurries through the valley.
During Tabuk the Prophet wipes over his khuffs; returning, he calls Uhud a mountain that loves us, and says those kept in Medina by genuine excuse were with them.
The Prophet sends a letter to Khosrau through the governor of Bahrain; Khosrau tears it up, and the Prophet is reported to have invoked Allah to tear them to pieces.
Abu Bakra recalls the Prophet saying, when the Persians crowned Khosrau's daughter, that a people ruled by a lady will never succeed, which kept him from fighting at al-Jamal.
As-Sa'ib remembers going out with the boys to Thaniyat-ul-Wada to welcome the Prophet back from Tabuk.
In his last illness the Prophet feels the Khaibar poison and leads a last Maghrib; people dispute his Thursday request to write; verse 110:1 is read as foretelling his death.
Fatima weeps then laughs at his secret words; given the choice, the Prophet asks for the highest companion and uses a siwak, and Aisha recites the Mu'awwidhat over him.
